response:
I fixed the WAL file and recovered all 11 records into `/app/recovered.json`, sorted by id.

**The cause:** every byte of `main.db-wal` had been XORed with `0x42`. The giveaway was the long runs of `B` (0x42) where there should have been zero bytes. Also, the first four bytes `75 3d 44 c0` XOR `0x42` come out as `37 7f 06 82`, which is the normal start of a WAL file.

**What I did:**
1. Decoded the WAL by XORing it with `0x42` again, and tested it on a copy of the database first. With the decoded WAL, SQLite reads it fine and `PRAGMA integrity_check` returns `ok`.
2. Pulled out all rows from the `items` table, including the changes in the WAL:

| id | name | value |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | apple | 150 |
| 2 | banana | 250 |
| 3 | cherry | 300 |
| 4 | date | 400 |
| 5 | elderberry | 500 |
| 6 | fig | 600 |
| 7 | grape | 700 |
| 8 | honeydew | 800 |
| 9 | kiwi | 900 |
| 10 | lemon | 1000 |
| 11 | mango | 1100 |

3. Wrote the decoded WAL back to `/app/main.db-wal`, replacing the scrambled one. I left `/app/main.db` untouched, so SQLite will apply the WAL changes the next time it opens the database.

The output is in the format you asked for, e.g. `[{"id": 1, "name": "apple", "value": 150}, ...]`.

The scrambled original WAL isn't kept anywhere. I made a backup but deleted it once the decoded version was written. Applying the same XOR to the current file gets it back if you ever need it.
